newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Privatisation plan soon for Israel's El Al airline.
newsitem.headline: Privatisation plan soon for Israel's El Al airline.

text.p: Israel's Transport Ministry said on Tuesday the committee charged with crafting a privatisation plan for state-owned El Al Israel Airlines would present the programme in 10 days.
"The programme will be presented...(in) 10 days," spokesman Avner Ovadiah told Reuters. He refused to elaborate on what the plan might entail.
There are obstacles in the path of the long-awaited privatisation.

On Monday, parliament's finance and labour and social affairs committees issued a joint statement after a hearing demanding that the government not decide on privatisation until it had ensured workers' rights, "including setting aside the necessary monies in a separate account".
They also demanded the government not even discuss the privatisation until it held "detailed negotiations with the El Al workers' representatives and reached an agreement with them".
Israel has long wanted to privatise El Al but a ban on flying on the Jewish sabbath and high security costs have deterred investors.
Ovadiah confirmed to Reuters that at Monday's hearing Transport Minister Yitzhak Levy said he would not consider any privatisation plan that allowed flights on the Jewish sabbath.
"He said even after privatisation, El Al will not fly on the sabbath," Ovadiah said.

The government controls 100 percent of the carrier. The airline, profitable for most of the last decade, is expected to post a huge loss for 1996. El Al has estimated its losses could reach $100 million for 1996. It expects the losses due to a drop in tourism following Islamic militant attacks, and higher fuel costs.
Newspaper reports have said it expects to lose $40 million in 1997.
